title: Genome-wide association analyses highlight the neuronal contribution to multiple sclerosis susceptibility.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py found no PMCID, supplement, accessions or NCBI links. GWAS Catalog (genome-wide association study catalogue) v2 API returned 0 studies for PMID 42706309. I read the medRxiv preprint's full text (PMC11643295): it has no data availability statement, and its only supplement is a 7.4 MB docx. The IMSGC (International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium) summary-statistics page is a request form with identity validation, a stated research aim and a no-redistribution agreement. The Nature page redirected to a login and medRxiv returned 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 20,831 cases, 729,220 controls, 236 non-MHC (major histocompatibility complex) variants and 76 candidate genes come from the abstract. The preprint text says the cohorts are the IMSGC, UK Biobank, eMERGE-III and All of Us, all of them controlled-access for individual-level data.

a1_downloadable.note: Individual-level genotypes (UK Biobank, All of Us, eMERGE via dbGaP, IMSGC) all need an access application. IMSGC summary statistics need a request form with identity validation (checked on imsgc.net). There is no GWAS Catalog deposit for this PMID (checked the API).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked against files. Per-person case/control status exists only in the controlled cohorts. Summary statistics give association p-values, not a measured label, so any variant-level target such as 'causal' would have to be constructed.

a5_enough_rows.note: The paper reports 20,831 cases, but those people are not accessible. Row count not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Individual-level genotypes from 750k people would not fit on a laptop. Summary statistics (~10M SNPs) would, but they are gated.

a8_label_provenance.note: Case status comes from ICD (diagnosis) codes in biobanks. Variant-level 'causal gene' calls are outputs of colocalisation and fine-mapping models, which would make them circular labels.

existing_models.name: The paper's own MS polygenic score (genetic risk score), built from non-MHC SNPs
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on IMSGC+UKBB+AoU and tested on held-out eMERGE-III, according to the preprint; numbers not extracted.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The score is optimised for European ancestry and is weaker in other ancestries.

existing_models.name: Machine-learning MS classifiers on UK Biobank genotypes (IJMS 2025, doi 10.3390/ijms26052085)
existing_models.score_and_split: Seen only in a search snippet: logistic regression was more stable than deep learning. Numbers not retrieved.

honest_claim_h3: Not reached: rejected at Part A because the data is not openly downloadable.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's genetic variants to predict their multiple sclerosis risk, and test whether it transfers across ancestries.
plain_idea.train_on: Genotypes of MS patients and controls from biobanks (the paper reports 20,831 cases and 729,220 controls; not verified, because the data is controlled-access).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a person has an MS diagnosis, taken from diagnosis codes in their medical records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Better risk prediction outside European ancestry would help MS genetics groups, but it needs individual-level data that sits behind access applications.

ml_idea: Considered: cross-ancestry MS risk prediction from genotypes, or prioritising causal variants from summary statistics. Neither is possible without controlled-access data or gated IMSGC summary statistics.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the summary statistics are openly deposited in the GWAS Catalog. They were not (0 studies for PMID 42706309).

verdict_reason: A1 fails. Individual-level data sits in controlled-access biobanks (UK Biobank, All of Us, dbGaP for eMERGE, IMSGC), and the summary statistics are behind an IMSGC request form with identity checks, not in the GWAS Catalog. A GWAS also offers no measured per-item label for modelling.
